NFC Authenticator Privacy Policy

Effective: October 30, 2026
Developer: Lukas Voegtle

Overview

The developer operates no authentication backend and receives no registration or authentication data. The app has no advertising, analytics, or tracking SDK. Transfers occur only when the user deliberately registers with a provider, explicitly renews a registration, or presents the phone to an NFC terminal. The app sends no background heartbeat and does not periodically contact providers.

Data stored locally

For each approved service and authentication profile, the app stores the service domain and disclosure metadata, approved fields and purposes, policy and deletion links, provider certificate fingerprint, approval and last-confirmed expiration times, a provider-issued opaque credential reference, and profile-specific credentials. Signing keys are not reused across services or profiles. Authentication attempts, assertions, NFC session keys, and access tokens are kept only in memory.

Transfers

Before registration, the app shows the recipient, operator, certificate-verified domain, exact requested fields and purposes, policy and deletion links, authentication profile, and registration lifetime. Registration requires “Agree and register.” Manual renewal requires a separate confirmation and sends only a one-time proof signed by the already approved service-specific credential. Online registration and renewal use HTTPS with the selected provider. During NFC use, authenticated application-layer encryption protects the phone-to-terminal hop, and the selected terminal submits the signed approval to its provider bridge over HTTPS. The provider and its terminal or proxy infrastructure are the intended recipient and can process the approved data; the app developer and unrelated network intermediaries do not receive plaintext. No undisclosed field is sent. Limited HTTPS requests fetch provider metadata, check that the service policy is accessible, and perform a user-requested registration or renewal.

Independent services

Each recipient controls subsequent processing under its own policy. Domain-certificate verification proves control of the service domain; it does not certify the named operator or legal sufficiency of its policy.

Retention and deletion

The app displays the last expiration confirmed during registration or explicit renewal. Providers may extend their authoritative server-side expiry after verified authentication; the offline phone cannot observe that terminal-to-provider result, so its date may be earlier. Local registrations remain until deleted in the app, app storage is cleared, or the app is uninstalled. Android backup is disabled. Local deletion removes the record and profile-specific signing key, but not the service’s copy; use its displayed deletion instructions. An expired provider registration must be registered again.

Security and logs

Private signing keys are held by Android Keystore. The app accepts only protocol version 4 encrypted traffic. Logs do not contain names, identifiers, keys, plaintext, or decrypted registration/authentication data.

Contact

App privacy requests: https://github.com/voegtlel/nfcauth/issues. Service data requests must use that service’s deletion contact.

Published policy: https://voegtlel.github.io/nfcauth/privacy-policy.html
